sources_considered.why: Controlled comparisons test whether supplying entity-state supervision improves coherence in BART and GPT-3.
Additional narrow intervention evidence, but it does not compare the proposed cause with other principal causes of GPT failures.
Causal interventions concern a specialized Othello model, not the outputs at issue.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Belinda Z. Li, Maxwell Nye, and Jacob Andreas

receipt.public_excerpt: we use entity states as auxiliary supervision to improve LMs ability to perform this reasoning under both fine-tuning and prompting.

evidence_items.explanation: Providing state supervision improves performance on TextWorld and TRIP, supporting a causal contribution from state reasoning. The experiments neither establish that representations were absent nor rank this mechanism as the principal cause of general GPT failures.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved experiment establishes the proposed mechanism as the principal cause across the claimed error population.
Adding state supervision changes available information and training or prompting; improvement does not establish complete prior absence of representations.
The cited word-problem failures were not directly subjected to causal intervention.
